system_thesis_interpretation: RML is a substantially better candidate instrument than the finite symbolic tables because it makes public actions stateful, forces connected old/new dependencies, adds a prospectively committed unwitnessed edge, and places the useful-memory test beyond a mechanically defined context boundary. The proposed common-deck DEV study can test the narrower chain public action/outcome record -> target-blind proposal and chronological admission -> compiled memory -> bounded reconstruction -> later executed action while holding experience fixed. Authentic-history, binding-shuffle, and twin interventions can establish that later behavior depends on world-specific action/outcome content. They do not establish that the agent learned which experience to acquire: the source actions are scripted, evaluation is write-isolated, and no memory assignment changes later evidence. Therefore this pilot is an experience-conditioned representation/use and constructive-action assay, not the action -> better evidence -> later memory -> later action experiential-learning flywheel. The proposal's claim firewall mostly respects that distinction, but its title and system-thesis language should not let a fixed-deck DEV pass be summarized as developmental experiential learning. The one fluid/thermal pack can at most de-risk an instrument and estimate component headroom; it cannot validate the paper-facing benchmark, cross-pack generality, post-native growth, baseline saturation, or a weights claim.
graph_delta_interpretation: The CPU -> gold-thinker/text -> conditional-LoRA partial order is scientifically sensible: it prevents transport work from masking a broken world, controller, or compiler. The graph nevertheless grants one ratification enough scope to build a new world and later execute model and LoRA stages before the exact world DSL, renderer, model/tokenizer/chat template, usable-context computation, prompts, operation schemas, source schedule, target counts, writer budgets, native baselines, LoRA recipe, and resource ceiling exist as bound artifacts. A fresh independent review at RML08 is a technical gate, not a substitute for a new exact human authorization over newly created scientific bytes. The highest-information feasible next graph is narrower: exact CPU RML world/target/twin/Bayes/program references and non-model fixtures; freeze and independently review their evidence; then create a new predecessor-bound proposal for the minimum gold-thinker and learned-writer/text factorial. LoRA should remain a separate third authority node after the text evidence is frozen. Additional missing graph nodes are an explicit writer-validity gate, a prospective-schema incremental-value gate, and an honest native graph/program baseline gate. Without them, the learned-text node combines proposal quality, support, compilation, retrieval, and resolver effects and cannot assign organ credit.
loop_delta_interpretation: The CPU loop targets the right threats but is not executable from the bound prose alone: 'many' lives, connected-program grammar, twin coupling, exact legal-plan enumeration, selection-conditioned no-life Bayes, J/P/X necessity, growth metrics, and runtime bounds are unspecified. The common-deck loop properly isolates memory representation/use, but because its source policy is fixed it does not test policy-selected experience or self-improvement. Within-item THINK outcomes test ordinary replanning, not durable learning, because evaluation cannot write back. The learned text loop also lacks a writer-specific loop that freezes proposal samples before outcomes, quantifies proposal precision/coverage/calibration, and compares learned proposals with deterministic witnessed atoms, gold-supported atoms, and an explicit program learner before compiler/read effects. The LoRA loop is appropriately conditional and same-corpus in intent, but should bind the exact semantic atom set, query catalog, clean-base control, candidate construction cost, unaided parser, training recipe, rank/capacity point, and failure semantics; otherwise recognition-assisted fidelity can be carried by candidate scans or the clean base. Recurrent SLEEP cadence is not manipulated here and must receive no cadence credit.
claim_delta_interpretation: The explicit DEV/non-claim firewall is a major strength. A positive one-pack result would support only that a particular rendered fluid/thermal DEV instrument has headroom and that a frozen protocol can use world-specific fixed-deck action/outcome history through a particular compiled-memory pipeline. It would not establish the RML benchmark as paper-ready, developmental scaling, strong experiential learning, autonomous discovery, DREAM necessity, SLEEP cadence value, a parametric moat, LoRA superiority, or the flywheel. Retiring PCFL/FeltCraft from the intended headline is a design choice, not evidence that RML is already the paper-facing benchmark. LoRA can receive only same-corpus transport/access credit, and even that requires clean-base, recognition-assisted, unaided, capacity, and query-work disclosures. If native graph or program induction wins, the scientifically correct outcome is that explicit structure dominates in this phase; if learned text works and LoRA loses, retain only the explicit compilation/use result. All result language must say fixed common deck, one-pack DEV, nested targets, and no population inference.
visibility_matrix_interpretation: The matrix captures the headline firewall—THINK gets the fresh public item, DREAM gets target-blind replay, SLEEP cannot see evaluation, and hidden truth stays offline—but its four information classes are too coarse for an executable leakage proof. 'Public life slice' must be decomposed into event content, source-policy schedule, era/checkpoint markers, renderer choices, world/life/split IDs, selection/rejection metadata, and future suffixes. 'Supported memory and provenance' should distinguish atom content from claim IDs, status history, root topology, support counts, retrieval scores, and selector receipts; DREAM may need bounded atom content and permitted public roots but should not see global topology or status-derived importance. SLEEP_COMPILER should consume a sealed eligible-status manifest, not raw later outcomes or an opportunity to redo the comparator. The matrix also omits source policy, target generator, writer, baseline builders/native graph/program learner, reader backend, LoRA trainer, and model-call runtime as stages, even though those are major leakage surfaces. THINK's cell conflates current ordinary within-item outcomes, which may support immediate replanning, with target completion/scorer outcomes and prior evaluation records, which must remain forbidden. Exact field-level taints and collision tests should cover all these stages before any model call.
acceptance_test_interpretation: RML01 correctly requires exact scope and ordering, but the requested scope is itself too broad because one approval conditionally authorizes later model/LoRA work whose exact scientific bytes do not yet exist. RML02 names the right world properties, yet it needs exact per-target plan-enumeration algorithms, J bridge counterfactuals, an atoms-only P ceiling, X pre-sealing, minimum unique-root/interaction increments, sample counts, rejection rules, and CPU/runtime budgets. RML03 should use a frozen uncurated suite and a Bayes controller conditioned on the complete target/world selection algorithm; every primary stratum and twin pair should have a legal plan and nontrivial posterior, not merely aggregate thresholds. RML04 is strong on chronology and isolation but needs exclusive writer authority, claim-type separating evidence, proposal precision/coverage/calibration, answer-injection sensitivity tests, and finer taints for schedules, IDs, selectors, baseline builders, readers, and training. RML05 is a useful controller factorial, but gold atoms and gold schema must be separately defined; the nonadaptive condition must commit queries before reads; generic recurrent thresholds need per-stratum reporting, model-call seeds, a direct-closure definition, and uncertainty or stability criteria suitable for tiny DEV. RML06 has the right baseline roster, but implementations/interfaces, writer budgets, common versus native channels, and program-family knowledge are unbound. '70% of gold gain' needs a named floor and denominator and must fail closed when the gold gain is zero or negative; the .10 baseline rule needs per-stratum and resource-qualified reporting. Add deterministic witnessed-atom compiler, gold-lifecycle compiler, dreamless direct builder, atoms-without-schema, and learned-proposal interventions so downstream text value does not become DREAM credit. RML07 is directionally correct but must be mechanically unreachable until RML05/RML06 evidence passes even though those tests are currently labeled required_before scientific_claim; it needs clean-base and direct-QA controls, exact candidate/query work, fixed rank/recipe, assisted versus unaided success definitions, and failure-as-zero semantics. RML08 correctly makes reviewer rejection binding, but review cannot authorize scientific bytes never ratified; repaired or newly frozen model-stage inputs should require a new predecessor-bound change and human decision. RML09 is an appropriate terminal firewall and should additionally lint 'experiential learning', 'paper-facing benchmark', 'developmental', and 'post-native improvement' unless their future claim-specific gates are actually met.
assumptions: No RML implementation, model result, or performance evidence exists at interpretation time.
The one-pack DEV study uses at most four counterfactual world-life pairs and treats targets, calls, dream samples, and adapter seeds as nested rather than independent.
The source policy in the proposed DEV common deck is scripted, target-blind, nonexhaustive, and identical across arms; therefore experience acquisition is not an estimand.
L_native, the primary backbone, tokenizer, chat template, prompts, world DSL, and compute envelope are not yet byte-bound by the change's context.
Hidden programs, proofs, target construction metadata, and evaluation scores remain available only to isolated noncognitive generation/scoring/audit processes.
Any future on-policy, multi-pack, locked, LOOP-training, external, publication, or claim work requires a new architecture change and human ratification.

ambiguities.question: Which exact model revision, tokenizer, chat template, maximum-position behavior, prompt/state/workspace/output reserves, and empirical procedure define L_native?
ambiguities.impact: The 0.5x/2x/4x/8x schedule, post-native status, world length, cost, and feasibility are undefined and can change materially with the chosen backbone.

ambiguities.question: What exact fluid/thermal state machine, causal-program grammar, higher-order law family, exception semantics, legal action enumeration, target generator, and structural rejection rule are authorized?
ambiguities.impact: Solvability, necessity, twin construction, Bayes inference, leakage, and implementation effort cannot be independently reproduced from the current prose.

ambiguities.question: What exact frozen source schedule is nonexhaustive and outcome-blind, and what guarantees that it supplies sufficient but non-answer-bearing evidence for J/P/X without encoding generator structure?
ambiguities.impact: The common deck could be either underinformative or a designer-curated curriculum whose schedule leaks the latent program.

ambiguities.question: What exact counterfactual deletion/intervention certifies J, what atom-only and witnessed-graph ceiling certifies P, and what pre-exception sealing plus information-gathering necessity certifies X?
ambiguities.impact: Successful action could remain separable retrieval, target-local reacquisition, or stored-schema execution rather than connected constructive use.

ambiguities.question: Are higher-order law classes, descriptors, prediction slots, candidate schemas, and held-out productions exposed to DREAM or the explicit program learner, and which productions/laws are held out across world-lives?
ambiguities.impact: P may measure inference inside a designer-supplied finite schema or generator familiarity rather than prospectively learned abstraction from experience.

ambiguities.question: What are the exact DREAM inputs, operation/sample budgets, proposal identity, prediction/deadline schema, claim-type separating panels, independent-root requirements, and exclusive status writers?
ambiguities.impact: A spraying or underdetermined writer could earn support from one later match, and downstream text performance would not reveal proposal precision, coverage, or calibration.

ambiguities.question: What exact query schema, candidate universe, return bytes, read/operation/action caps, anchoring rule, workspace size, malformed-output rule, and model generation configuration define generic recurrent THINK?
ambiguities.impact: Query scaffolding, candidate recognition, hidden scans, or an answer-bearing controller could carry performance attributed to memory.

ambiguities.question: Which pinned implementations and native interfaces define raw RAG, native witnessed graph, A-MEM, reflection, procedural memory, and generator-aware program induction, and what generator knowledge may each use?
ambiguities.impact: The strongest-baseline threshold is not reproducible, and a handicapped graph/program baseline could manufacture apparent memory value.

ambiguities.question: Relative to which floor and over which strata/cuts is '70% of gold gain' computed, and what happens when gold gain is zero, negative, or heterogeneous?
ambiguities.impact: The learned-text promotion threshold is mathematically incomplete and can yield unstable or favorable interpretations.

ambiguities.question: How many world pairs, targets, model generations, and adapter seeds feed each gate, and what uncertainty, repeatability, or worst-stratum rule accompanies .85, .35, 70%, .10, .90, and -.05 thresholds?
ambiguities.impact: A four-pair DEV point estimate can create high false-go or false-stop rates even if it is not used for a paper claim.

ambiguities.question: What exact corpus identity, views, negative examples, candidate catalog, clean-base comparison, training recipe, rank, precision, token budget, query work, assisted-read protocol, and unaided parser define transport?
ambiguities.impact: Recognition menus, clean-base priors, changing capacity, or exhaustive candidate scans could be mistaken for value retained in weights.

ambiguities.question: What bounded CPU generation/oracle time, model-call count, writer-token budget, adapter training budget, disk footprint, and wall-clock ceiling make the proposed 8x-native one-pack pilot feasible?
ambiguities.impact: The proposal may authorize an open-ended world-building and inference program rather than a days-scale highest-information pilot.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The staged one-pack concept is directionally right, but the exact requested scope is not the highest-information feasible next authorization because it bundles CPU invention, model science, native baselines, and LoRA transport before their executable contracts exist.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The prior exact PCFL bundle correctly separated CPU reference construction from later model authority. Here a technical review can release GPU work under a broad earlier ratification even though model revisions, prompts, schemas, baselines, budgets, and recipes are not bound. This weakens both scientific auditability and stopping value.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Ratify only an RML D0 CPU reference scope first. Require a new predecessor-bound architecture change and human ratification for the exact gold-thinker/writer/text DEV bundle, and a third one for LoRA after frozen text evidence passes.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: RML v1 does not test action-selection-driven experiential learning or the full action/outcome learning flywheel; it tests experience-conditioned memory formation and use under a supplied common deck.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: Source actions do not depend on memory, evaluation is disposable, and no later evidence distribution changes. Authentic binding can cause later action without showing that the agent learned to acquire better experience.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Use fixed-deck representation/use language everywhere in this change, reserve 'experiential learning' and 'flywheel' for the randomized on-policy study, and add those terms to the claim linter.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposed target-necessity language is not yet sufficient to ensure J/P/X identify connected constructive use.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: J deletion must eliminate every legal recent-only plan; P needs a quantified atoms-only and witnessed-graph ceiling; X needs target sealing plus a necessity proof for discriminating information and backtracking. The change names these properties but does not bind exact certifiers.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Create executable per-target exhaustive certificates and adversarial shortcut controllers before model work; fail the generator on any uncertified target rather than relying on cohort averages.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: Post-native status and the 8x lifetime axis are not scientifically defined until the exact model and usable-context procedure are frozen.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: A convenient imposed cap is not native context, while a modern long-native model can make 8x prohibitively large. Choosing the backbone after seeing engineering constraints can change both difficulty and claim geometry.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Bind the primary model/tokenizer/template and mechanical L_native calculation in D0, precompute event counts and cost at every cut, and prohibit post-hoc context capping or backbone substitution.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: Precommitment alone does not establish learned prospective schema; the supplied law class, descriptors, selection rule, or generator-aware controller may carry the abstraction.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: One pack and a small DEV set cannot distinguish autonomous schema formation from inference inside a designer-provided finite grammar unless productions/laws and descriptor bindings are held out and atom-only/schema-shuffle controls are explicit.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Bind prospective prediction fields and deadlines; hold out complete law productions across lives; add atoms-without-schema, post-outcome leaked-schema ceiling, descriptor/schema binding shuffle, explicit gold schema, and generator-program baselines; require incremental P value over atoms.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: Declaring graph/program/A-MEM baselines is not enough to make them honest or reproducible.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The proposal does not pin implementations, native query/traversal interfaces, program-family knowledge, capacity points, or useful-compute/resource ledgers. The learned-text gate permits a .10 deficit but cannot be interpreted if the comparator is crippled or under-resourced.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Freeze each baseline's source/version, prompt, generator knowledge, native and common-channel interface, capacity grid, and resource vector before model calls; let graph/program wins stand without threshold relaxation.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: A downstream learned-text score is not an adequate verification of DREAM proposal quality or chronological support.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: It conflates writer recall/precision, proposal search, comparator adequacy, compiler formatting, retrieval, and THINK. Fixed proposal counts prevent unlimited search but do not prevent low-specificity claims or support from underdetermining evidence.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Add a pre-text writer-validity gate with exclusive writer matrix, claim-type separating panels, proposal precision/coverage/calibration, chronology, contradiction behavior, root diversity, prospective specificity, and answer-injection tests. Compare deterministic witnessed atoms, gold-supported atoms, and dreamless direct builders.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The current factorial can separate a broken generic thinker and LoRA transport, but it cannot identify DREAM necessity or SLEEP contribution.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: SLEEP is deterministic and DREAM/SLEEP learned text is bundled. A pass supports the whole compiled-memory protocol, not autonomous discovery, dream necessity, or recurrent sleep value.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: State bundled pipeline credit explicitly and add only the minimum organ controls needed for later claims: gold lifecycle, deterministic witnessed-atom compiler, learned writer with the same compiler, dreamless direct builder, and separately deferred recurrent-versus-batch cadence.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: LoRA conditionality is conceptually correct but not yet enforceable or attribution-complete.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: RML05/RML06 are labeled required_before scientific_claim rather than mechanically before the LoRA GPU stage, and transport lacks a bound clean-base, direct-QA, capacity, candidate-work, and unaided-read contract.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Make passing text manifests explicit prerequisites to any LoRA entry point, require new authority, freeze one corpus and recipe, include clean-base/direct-QA controls, report assisted and unaided reads separately, and treat linear candidate scans or growing rank as external search/storage rather than parametric access.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposed DEV thresholds are useful heuristics but are over-precise for at most four world pairs without stability rules.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: Targets and generations are nested, not replications. A point estimate can cross .85, .35, .10, or -.05 because of one pair, one target mix, or one model seed, and '70% gold gain' has no defined denominator edge case.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Treat gates as engineering decisions, report every pair/stratum, average nested seeds within pair, bind repeated-call stability or conservative intervals, define all denominators and failure cases, and forbid inferential or population language.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The proposal has not shown that a fluid/thermal world with exact Bayes, 6-12-step necessity, prospective laws, exceptions, twins, and 8x-native replay is a bounded days-scale pilot.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: World construction and exact validation may dominate model cost; the chosen native window can expand the source stream by orders of magnitude; writer calls and baseline implementations are not costed. 'One pack' limits breadth but not complexity.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Before scientific authorization, require a CPU performance/resource prototype with fixed counts and wall ceilings. If it fails, narrow D0 to J plus one prospective P law, preserve X for a second rung, and do not weaken necessity or leakage controls to meet schedule.

open_questions: Should authority be narrowed to CPU-only RML D0, with separate later human decisions for gold-thinker/text and LoRA after their exact bytes and predecessor evidence exist?
